Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Work & responsibility

recruit verb and noun

also recruits, recruitment, enlist, enrol, a new recruit, raw recruit, levy, draft, hold a draft, call-up, recruit troops

classical

Caes. BG 1.10 (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 37.46.10: sex mīlia familiārum cōnscrīberet (Lewis & Short)

cōnscrībō, cōnscrībere, cōnscrīpsī, cōnscrīptum

verb, third conjugation, transitive

enlist, enrol (soldiers, colonists, members)

To write together in a list: the standing word for enlisting troops, and for enrolling colonists or a class of citizens; hence patrēs cōnscrīptī. To hire staff is condūcere (see employ).

Other words

  • dēlēctum habēre — hold a levy, recruit troops

    verb phrase: dēlēctus (dīlēctus), dēlēctūs m.; habeō, habēre · also used · classical · Caes. BG 6.1: per lēgātōs dēlēctum habēre (Lewis & Short); Traupman 187: recruit troops (dīlēctum agere); Traupman 186: draft, dīlēctus; to hold a draft, dīlēctum habēre

    “A standing phrase for recruiting” (Lewis & Short); dēlēctum agere is post-Augustan. dēlēctus is the choosing and the levy itself (see choice).

  • tīrō, tīrōnis m. — a recruit, a new soldier; a beginner

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 11.39: tīrōnēs mīlitēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 187: recruit; Traupman 182: raw recruit, tīrō rudis

    Also a beginner at anything: in forō tīrō, new to the courts (Lewis & Short).

  • ascīscō (adscīscō), ascīscere, ascīvī, ascītum — take in, admit (as a member, a citizen, an ally)

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Arch. 4: nōn modo nōn sēgregandum ā numerō cīvium vērum etiam adscīscendum (Lewis & Short, s.v. sēgregō)

    For recruiting someone into a group by choice; see also adopt.

  • nōmen dare — give in one’s name, enlist (of the recruit)

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. nōmen: “to give in one’s name, be enrolled, enlist”; Traupman 186; Liv. 2.24: nē nōmina darent (Lewis & Short s.v. nōmen); Traupman 310

Examples

  • Nōn jam tīrō rudis sum!

    I’m no longer a raw recruit!Traupman 182

  • dīlēctum agere

    to recruit troopsTraupman 369

See also army, soldier, employ, choice, member, adopt.
